newsitem.title: MEXICO: Opposition ahead in Mexico City governor race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Opposition ahead in Mexico City governor race - poll.

text.p: A poll released on Monday shows the conservative opposition National Action Party (PAN) would have received 25.5 percent of the votes for governor of Mexico City, if the vote were held Monday.

The PAN would be ahead of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which would have received 21 percent of the vote, according to a poll published in the El Economista and El Diario de Monterrey newspapers.
The left-leaning Democratic Revolution Party (PRD) would have received 15.3 percent, the newspapers said. The poll was commissioned from the Mexican pollster Gabinete de Estudios de Opinion.
The poll was carried out on January 31 and February 1 among 400 people of voting age. It is considered to be accurate to within five percent 95 percent of the time.
Mexico City residents will vote for the first time this summer to elect a governor for the huge metropolis. Previously, the city chief, known as the mayor, has been hand picked by the president.
Electing a governor for the capital is part of Mexico's new drive for greater democracy. The vote will be held July 6, alongside key congressional elections and other state governorships.
